we propose a novel Bayesian optimization algorithm for reinforcement learning that can combine simulations and physical experiments, and show that it can find good control parameters with fewer experiments than a standard Bayesian optimization algorithm on the physical system.

(1) we propose to combine simulations and experiments in reinforcement learning using Bayesian optimization and (2) we demonstrate that this method can reduce the number of physical experiments needed to find a good control policy.

the question of whether it is better to do a few physical experiments or many simulations in order to learn a good control policy.
the question: how can we combine simulations and physical experiments to efficiently find good control policies?

we propose a method for reinforcement learning using Bayesian optimization, which can combine simulations and physical experiments to learn a good control policy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
simulations can be exploited to reduce the number of physical experiments in reinforcement-learning applications.
, for reinforcement learning, it is often more efficient to combine simulations with a small number of physical experiments than to rely on physical experiments alone.

, when simulations are available, we can reduce the number of experiments by up to 90% without sacrificing performance, which makes reinforcement learning practical for many real-life robotic systems.
